    rows_with_vals = [r for r in range(len(grid)) if any(grid[r])]
    if not rows_with_vals: return grid
    min_r, max_r = min(rows_with_vals), max(rows_with_vals)
    out = [row[:] for row in grid]
    sub = [grid[r] for r in range(min_r, max_r + 1)]
    for i, r in enumerate(range(min_r, max_r + 1)):
        out[r] = sub[len(sub) - 1 - i]
    # Wait, in input: row 1 is [0,0,3,3,0,0,0], row 2 is [0,0,3,3,0,0,0], row 3 is [0,9,9,9,9,0,0], row 4 is [0,9,9,9,9,0,0]
    # Reversing sub: row 4, row 3, row 2, row 1.
    # Row 4 is [0,9,9,9,9,0,0] -> becomes row 1!
    # Row 3 is [0,9,9,9,9,0,0] -> becomes row 2!
    # Row 2 is [0,0,3,3,0,0,0] -> becomes row 3!
    # Row 1 is [0,0,3,3,0,0,0] -> becomes row 4!
    # This matches the output perfectly!
    return out

    # In input, object 3 is on top of object 9.
    # In output, object 9 is on top of object 3.
    # This is equivalent to vertically flipping the stack.

    out = [row[:] for row in grid]
